scope: This discharges the abstract duplicate-character and separator premises: square product gives identical Galois signs, while any third square-product partner would complete a forbidden cubic orbit. It still assumes the selected roots, lifted point data, and transformed relations; it does not construct the specialized Semaev relation, prove torsion-to-division-polynomial vanishing, or establish the subexponential ECDLP runtime theorem.
statement: For the A equals zero short curve over a prime field, positive injective interval scales bounded by X with 3X less than p, one square-product collision, selected square roots in a finite Galois extension, lifted affine points, and the Galois-transformed point relations imply a nonidentity cubic CM ratio and an explicit Eisenstein norm that annihilates the chosen point.
